title: Expert discusses AI’s role in modern warfare
gist: Local news report on a Cameron University talk by CNAS executive VP Paul Scharre, who argues AI warfare is already here: Ukraine uses ~4 million drones a year, FPV drones carry terminal autonomy, and a decade of UN talks has produced no agreement beyond applying the law of war to autonomous weapons. (Most of the article body is stored in an encoded form in the raw text; it was decoded for extraction, so quotes are limited to the plain-text portion.)

insights.claim: Paul Scharre, executive vice president of the Center for a New American Security, argues that AI warfare is not a future scenario but is happening now, and that AI will transform the cognitive dimension of warfare.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
entities: Center for a New American Security
insights.so_what: Defense AI spend is a present-tense procurement theme, not a long-dated option; favors vendors already fielding systems.
insights.quote: The age of AI warfare is not some future thing
insights.locator: The military is already figuring out

insights.claim: According to Scharre, AI systems are currently playing roles in military conflicts in Gaza, Ukraine and Iran.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: Multiple live theaters act as combat-testing grounds that accelerate adoption and doctrine for AI-enabled weapons.

themes.theme: Drone mass and embedded autonomy in Ukraine

insights.claim: Scharre says Ukraine is using about 4 million drones a year, a scale he calls 'kind of crazy', showing drones are now used on a massive scale in warfare.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: Consumable drone volumes in the millions per year imply a high-throughput, low-cost munitions market and supply-chain demand (motors, cameras, batteries, chips).

insights.claim: Ukraine's first-person-view (FPV) drones stream live video from an onboard camera to a human pilot, who flies them as if sitting inside the drone, 'like a race car'.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: Cheap human-piloted FPV systems are the baseline that autonomy layers are being added onto.

insights.claim: Autonomy is already built into FPV drones so that once the pilot locks onto a target, the drone can take over and maneuver the strike itself — a terminal-guidance handoff from human to machine.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: Terminal autonomy defeats jamming of the pilot link; watch demand for onboard vision/targeting compute and software in small drones.

insights.claim: Scharre frames the central question of AI warfare as whether humans or machines should make life-or-death decisions, and what happens when a drone has as much autonomy as a soldier.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: The human-in-the-loop question will shape export rules, procurement requirements and ESG screening of defense-AI names.

insights.claim: Despite more than a decade of discussion at the United Nations, countries have only agreed that the law of war applies to autonomous weapons; there is no agreement on further action or on whether a treaty or regulation is needed.
insights.speaker: Eric Swanson eric.swanson@swoknews.com
insights.so_what: Absence of binding international limits means autonomy development proceeds largely unconstrained; low near-term regulatory risk for autonomous-weapons developers.
